668	def _can_create_in_workspace(username: str) -> bool:
669	    """
670	    True if *username* can create new resources in the request's workspace.
671	
672	    Always allows when workspaces are disabled. Otherwise requires a
673	    workspace-wide grant whose level has ``can_use`` (i.e. USE or MANAGE under
674	    the simplified two-tier workspace model). Resource-specific grants don't
675	    confer create rights — only workspace-wide grants do.
676	
677	    Querying with ``resource_type='workspace'`` restricts the resolver to the
678	    unified workspace-wide grant slot (``rp.resource_type='workspace'`` with
679	    ``rp.resource_pattern='*'``); resource-specific grants on concrete types
680	    don't satisfy this lookup.
681	
682	    Also honors ``auth_config.grant_default_workspace_access``: when enabled and
683	    the request workspace is the default workspace, an ungranted user inherits
684	    ``default_permission`` and can create iff that permission carries ``can_use``.
685	    """
686	    if not MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get():
687	        return True
688	
689	    workspace_name = workspace_context.get_request_workspace()
690	    if workspace_name is None:
691	        return False
692	
693	    user = store.get_user(username)
694	    perm = store.get_role_permission_for_resource(user.id, "workspace", "*", workspace_name)
695	    if perm is not None and perm.can_use:
696	        return True
697	    if perm is None and _user_inherits_default_workspace_grant(workspace_name):
698	        return get_permission(auth_config.default_permission).can_use
699	    return False
700

706	def _get_resource_workspace(
707	    resource_id: str,
708	    fetcher: Callable[[str], Any],
709	    resource_label: str,
710	    silent: bool = False,
711	) -> str | None:
712	    """
713	    Get the workspace name for a resource, using a cache to avoid repeated lookups.
714	
715	    The resource->workspace relationship is immutable, so caching is safe.
716	
717	    Args:
718	        silent: When True, suppress the lookup-failure warning. Set by
719	            non-authorization callers (e.g. listing endpoints) where a
720	            ``None`` return is an expected outcome for deleted resources
721	            rather than a security-relevant error.
722	    """
723	    # Use a cache key that includes the resource_label to avoid collisions between
724	    # experiments and registered models that might have the same ID/name.
725	    workspace_scope = (
726	        workspace_context.get_request_workspace() if MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get() else None
727	    )
728	    cache_key = (
729	        f"{resource_label}:{workspace_scope}:{resource_id}" if workspace_scope is not None else None
730	    )
731	
732	    if cache_key is not None and cache_key in _RESOURCE_WORKSPACE_CACHE:
733	        return _RESOURCE_WORKSPACE_CACHE[cache_key]
734	
735	    try:
736	        resource = fetcher(resource_id)
737	        workspace_name = getattr(resource, "workspace", None)
738	    except MlflowException as e:
739	        if not silent:
740	            _logger.warning(
741	                "Failed to determine workspace for %s '%s': %s. Denying access for security.",
742	                resource_label,
743	                resource_id,
744	                e,
745	            )
746	        workspace_name = None
747	
748	    if cache_key is None:
749	        cache_key = (
750	            f"{resource_label}:{workspace_name}:{resource_id}"
751	            if workspace_name is not None
752	            else f"{resource_label}:{resource_id}"
753	        )
754	
755	    _RESOURCE_WORKSPACE_CACHE[cache_key] = workspace_name
756	    return workspace_name

765	def _role_permission_for(
766	    username: str,
767	    resource_type: str,
768	    resource_key: str,
769	    workspace_lookup_id: str,
770	    workspace_fetcher: Callable[[str], Any],
771	    workspace_label: str,
772	) -> Callable[[], Permission | None]:
773	    """
774	    Build a callable that resolves a user's role-based permission on a specific resource,
775	    for use as ``role_permission_func`` in ``_get_role_permission_or_default``.
776	
777	    ``resource_key`` is the lookup key for ``role_permissions`` (may differ from the
778	    workspace-resolution id for composite resources, e.g. scorers use
779	    ``SqlAlchemyStore._scorer_pattern(experiment_id, scorer_name)`` as the role key
780	    but resolve the workspace via the parent experiment).
781	    """
782	
783	    def _role_perm() -> Permission | None:
784	        user = store.get_user(username)
785	        if MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get():
786	            workspace_name = _get_resource_workspace(
787	                workspace_lookup_id, workspace_fetcher, workspace_label
788	            )
789	            if workspace_name is None:
790	                # Workspace lookup failed with workspaces enabled — deny by returning
791	                # NO_PERMISSIONS (security: don't let resource_not_found silently become a
792	                # default-permission grant).
793	                return NO_PERMISSIONS
794	        else:
795	            # Workspaces disabled: every resource lives in the default workspace, which is
796	            # where grants are stored. Skip the tracking-store workspace lookup so resolution
797	            # honors the grant even when the tracking store has no data for the resource — e.g.
798	            # an --artifacts-only server that shares the auth DB but has no experiment data.
799	            workspace_name = DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_NAME
800	        perm = store.get_role_permission_for_resource(
801	            user.id, resource_type, resource_key, workspace_name
802	        )
803	        if perm is not None:
804	            return perm
805	        # No grant in the resolved workspace. With workspaces disabled, fall through
806	        # to the configured default. With workspaces enabled, deny — *unless* the
807	        # operator opted into ``grant_default_workspace_access`` and this is the
808	        # default workspace, in which case the user inherits ``default_permission``
809	        # so deployments that relied on the implicit auto-grant pre-simplification
810	        # don't lose resource-level access.
811	        if not MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get():
812	            return None
813	        # Only reachable with workspaces enabled — the guard above returns first when
814	        # disabled, so ``_user_inherits_default_workspace_grant`` (which touches the
815	        # workspace store) never runs on an artifacts-only / workspaces-disabled server.
816	        if _user_inherits_default_workspace_grant(workspace_name):
817	            return get_permission(auth_config.default_permission)
818	        return NO_PERMISSIONS
819	
820	    return _role_perm

848	        )
849	        if perm is not None:

854	        # above returns first when disabled, so the workspace-store lookup here never runs
855	        # on a workspaces-disabled server.
856	        if _user_inherits_default_workspace_grant(resolved_workspace):
857	            return get_permission(auth_config.default_permission)

860	    return _role_perm

1895	def _role_based_read_predicate(username: str, resource_type: str) -> Callable[[str], bool]:
1896	    """
1897	    Build a ``p(resource_id) -> bool`` predicate from ``username``'s role
1898	    grants in the active workspace. Max-style: any positive grant (specific or
1899	    wildcard) wins; ``NO_PERMISSIONS`` rows are ignored. Falls back to
1900	    ``default_permission.can_read`` when workspaces are disabled, otherwise to
1901	    deny.
1902	    """
1903	    workspace_name = (
1904	        workspace_context.get_request_workspace()
1905	        if MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get()
1906	        else DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_NAME
1907	    )
1908	    if workspace_name is None:
1909	        return lambda _resource_id: False
1910	
1911	    user = store.get_user(username)
1912	    readable: set[str] = set()
1913	    wildcard_can_read = False
1914	    for resource_pattern, permission in store.list_role_grants_for_user_in_workspace(
1915	        user.id, workspace_name, resource_type
1916	    ):
1917	        if not get_permission(permission).can_read:
1918	            continue
1919	        if resource_pattern == "*":
1920	            wildcard_can_read = True
1921	        else:
1922	            readable.add(resource_pattern)
1923	
1924	    default_can_read = get_permission(auth_config.default_permission).can_read
1925	    fallback = (
1926	        default_can_read
1927	        if (
1928	            not MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get()
1929	            or _user_inherits_default_workspace_grant(workspace_name)
1930	        )
1931	        else False
1932	    )
1933	
1934	    def predicate(resource_id: str) -> bool:
1935	        return resource_id in readable or wildcard_can_read or fallback
1936	
1937	    return predicate

3644	def _is_known_ungated_route(path: str) -> bool:
3645	    # Anchor markers to a segment boundary: "/mlflow/issues" matches "/mlflow/issues"
3646	    # and "/mlflow/issues/..." but not "/mlflow/issues-other".
3647	    for marker in _KNOWN_UNGATED_ROUTE_MARKERS:
3648	        if marker.endswith("/"):
3649	            if marker in path:
3650	                return True
3651	            continue
3652	        start = 0
3653	        while (idx := path.find(marker, start)) != -1:
3654	            end = idx + len(marker)
3655	            if end == len(path) or path[end] == "/":
3656	                return True

5147	class GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware:
5148	    """
5149	    Graphene middleware that enforces per-object authorization for GraphQL queries.
5150

5151	    This middleware checks user permissions before resolving protected fields.
5152	    It integrates with MLflow's basic-auth permission system.
5153	    """
5154	
5155	    PROTECTED_FIELDS = {
5156	        "mlflowGetExperiment",
5157	        "mlflowGetRun",
5158	        "mlflowListArtifacts",
5159	        "mlflowGetMetricHistoryBulkInterval",
5160	        "mlflowSearchRuns",
5161	        "mlflowSearchDatasets",
5162	        "mlflowSearchModelVersions",
5163	    }
5164	    # Nested fields, keyed by (parent GraphQL type, field name). ``run.modelVersions``
5165	    # (reachable via mlflowGetRun / mlflowSearchRuns) resolves through the unfiltered search
5166	    # implementation, so it needs the same per-model filter as the top-level search. Keying
5167	    # on the parent type keeps the same-named, already-filtered sub-field of
5168	    # ``MlflowSearchModelVersionsResponse`` out of the middleware.
5169	    PROTECTED_NESTED_FIELDS = {("MlflowRunExtension", "modelVersions")}
5170	
5171	    def resolve(self, next, root, info, **args):
5172	        """
5173	        Middleware resolve function called for every field resolution.
5174	
5175	        Args:
5176	            next: The next resolver in the chain
5177	            root: The root value object
5178	            info: GraphQL resolve info containing field name and context
5179	            args: Field arguments as keyword arguments
5180	
5181	        Returns:
5182	            The resolved value or an error response
5183	        """
5184	        field_name = info.field_name
5185	
5186	        if (
5187	            field_name not in self.PROTECTED_FIELDS
5188	            and (info.parent_type.name, field_name) not in self.PROTECTED_NESTED_FIELDS
5189	        ):
5190	            return next(root, info, **args)
5191	
5192	        try:
5193	            authorization = authenticate_request()
5194	            if isinstance(authorization, Response):
5195	                return None
5196	            username = authorization.username
5197	
5198	            if store.get_user(username).is_admin:
5199	                return next(root, info, **args)
5200	        except Exception:
5201	            _logger.warning("GraphQL authorization failed: auth system error", exc_info=True)
5202	            return None
5203	
5204	        try:
5205	            if not self._check_authorization(field_name, args, username):
5206	                _logger.debug(f"GraphQL authorization denied for {field_name} by user {username}")
5207	                return None
5208	        except MlflowException:
5209	            return None
5210	        except Exception:
5211	            _logger.warning(f"GraphQL authorization error for {field_name}", exc_info=True)
5212	            return None
5213	
5214	        result = next(root, info, **args)
5215	        return self._post_resolve(field_name, result, username) if result is not None else None
5216	
5217	    def _check_authorization(self, field_name: str, args: dict[str, Any], username: str) -> bool:
5218	        """
5219	        Check if the user is authorized to access the requested field.
5220	
5221	        Args:
5222	            field_name: The GraphQL field being resolved
5223	            args: The field arguments
5224	            username: The authenticated username
5225	
5226	        Returns:
5227	            True if authorized, False otherwise
5228	        """
5229	        input_obj = args.get("input")
5230	        if input_obj is None:
5231	            # No input means no specific resource to check
5232	            return True

5320	def _authenticate_fastapi_request(request: StarletteRequest) -> User | None:
5321	    """
5322	    Authenticate request using Basic Auth.
5323	
5324	    External clients send real username/password credentials. Server-spawned job
5325	    subprocesses (e.g., online scoring) send the internal gateway token as the
5326	    password; when it matches, the user is trusted without calling
5327	    ``store.authenticate_user()``.
5328	
5329	    Args:
5330	        request: The Starlette/FastAPI Request object.
5331	
5332	    Returns:
5333	        User object if authentication succeeds, None otherwise.
5334	    """
5335	    request_path = get_routed_asgi_path(request)
5336	    static_prefix = os.environ.get(STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, "").rstrip("/")
5337	    if static_prefix and request_path.startswith(static_prefix):
5338	        request_path = request_path[len(static_prefix) :]
5339	
5340	    # On /gateway/ routes, a coding agent's own provider key occupies the standard
5341	    # Authorization header (forwarded upstream), so MLflow credentials ride in a dedicated
5342	    # header. Prefer it there; fall back to Authorization for backward compat.
5343	    auth = None
5344	    if request_path.startswith("/gateway/"):
5345	        auth = request.headers.get(MLFLOW_GATEWAY_AUTH_HEADER)
5346	    # Treat a missing OR empty header as absent so an empty X-MLflow-Authorization
5347	    # does not shadow a valid Authorization header.
5348	    if not auth:
5349	        auth = request.headers.get("Authorization")
5350	
5351	    # Neither header present — unauthenticated.
5352	    if not auth:
5353	        return None
5354	    try:
5355	        scheme, credentials = auth.split()
5356	        if scheme.lower() != "basic":
5357	            return None
5358	        decoded = base64.b64decode(credentials).decode("ascii")
5359	        username, _, password = decoded.partition(":")
5360	
5361	        # Check if this is a trusted internal request from a job subprocess.
5362	        # The server generates a random token at startup and passes it to workers
5363	        # via _MLFLOW_INTERNAL_GATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN. When the password matches that
5364	        # token, we trust the username without calling store.authenticate_user().
5365	        # Restrict to /gateway/ routes only so the token cannot be used as a
5366	        # master password on other endpoints (e.g. /v1/traces, /ajax-api/).
5367	        internal_token = _MLFLOW_INTERNAL_GATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN.get()
5368	        if (
5369	            internal_token
5370	            and request_path.startswith("/gateway/")
5371	            and secrets.compare_digest(password, internal_token)
5372	        ):
5373	            return store.get_user(username)
5374	
5375	        return _authenticate_cached(username, password)
5376	    except Exception:
5377	        return None

5380	def _authenticate_custom_for_fastapi(
5381	    request: StarletteRequest,
5382	) -> User | StarletteResponse | None:
5383	    """Bridge custom authorization_function into the FastAPI middleware path.
5384	
5385	    Custom auth functions (configured via ``authorization_function`` in auth config)
5386	    are written against Flask's request context (``flask.request``). This function
5387	    creates a synthetic Flask request context from the Starlette request, invokes the
5388	    custom function within it, and translates the result back.
5389	
5390	    Returns:
5391	        - A ``User`` if authentication succeeds.
5392	        - A Starlette ``Response`` if the custom auth function returned a Flask Response
5393	          (converted to preserve status code, headers, and body).
5394	        - ``None`` if authentication fails (no username / unknown user).
5395	
5396	    Raises:
5397	        MlflowException: If the custom auth function returns an unsupported type,
5398	            matching Flask ``_before_request`` failure semantics.
5399	    """
5400	    headers = dict(request.headers)
5401	    with app.test_request_context(
5402	        path=request.url.path,
5403	        method=request.method,
5404	        headers=headers,
5405	        query_string=request.url.query or "",
5406	    ):
5407	        authorization = authenticate_request()
5408	        if isinstance(authorization, Response):
5409	            return _flask_response_to_starlette(authorization)
5410	        if not isinstance(authorization, Authorization):
5411	            # Match Flask `_before_request`: unsupported plugin return types are an
5412	            # internal misconfiguration, not an authentication failure (401).
5413	            raise MlflowException(
5414	                f"Unsupported result type from {auth_config.authorization_function}: "
5415	                f"'{type(authorization).__name__}'",
5416	                INTERNAL_ERROR,
5417	            )
5418	        username = authorization.username
5419	        if not username:
5420	            return None
5421	        try:
5422	            return store.get_user(username)
5423	        except Exception:
5424	            return None

5427	def _flask_response_to_starlette(flask_resp: Response) -> StarletteResponse:
5428	    """Convert a Flask/Werkzeug Response to a Starlette Response.
5429	
5430	    Preserves status code, headers (including multi-value headers like Set-Cookie),
5431	    and body so custom auth functions can return meaningful error responses
5432	    (e.g., 403 with a custom message, or a redirect) that get forwarded to the
5433	    client unchanged.
5434	    """
5435	    _hop_by_hop_headers = {"content-length", "transfer-encoding"}
5436	    response = StarletteResponse(
5437	        content=flask_resp.get_data(),
5438	        status_code=flask_resp.status_code,
5439	    )
5440	    for key, value in flask_resp.headers:
5441	        if key.lower() in _hop_by_hop_headers:
5442	            continue
5443	        response.headers.append(key, value)
5444	    return response

5447	def _extract_gateway_endpoint_name(path: str, body: dict[str, Any] | None) -> str | None:
5448	    """Extract endpoint name from gateway routes."""
5449	    # Pattern 1: /gateway/{endpoint_name}/mlflow/invocations
5450	    if match := re.match(r"^/gateway/([^/]+)/mlflow/invocations$", path):
5451	        return match.group(1)
5452	
5453	    # Pattern 2-6: Passthrough routes (endpoint in request body as "model")
5454	    if path in _ROUTES_NEEDING_BODY:
5455	        if body:
5456	            return body.get("model")
5457	        return None
5458	
5459	    # Pattern 7-8: Gemini routes (endpoint in URL path)
5460	    if match := re.match(r"^/gateway/gemini/v1beta/models/([^/:]+):generateContent$", path):
5461	        return match.group(1)
5462	    if match := re.match(r"^/gateway/gemini/v1beta/models/([^/:]+):streamGenerateContent$", path):
5463	        return match.group(1)
5464	
5465	    # Pattern 9: Raw proxy route (/gateway/proxy/{endpoint_name}/{path:path})
5466	    if match := re.match(r"^/gateway/proxy/([^/]+)/", path):
5467	        return match.group(1)
5468	
5469	    return None

5646	def _backfill_readable_mcp_results(
5647	    can_read: Callable[[str], bool],
5648	    readable: list[dict[str, Any]],
5649	    max_results: int,

5654	) -> str | None:

5657	        page = fetch_page(next_token)

5664	            consumed += 1
5665	            if can_read(get_name(item)):

5669	        else:
5670	            next_token = page.token
5671	        if isinstance(next_token, bytes):
5672	            next_token = next_token.decode("utf-8")
5673	    return next_token

5887	def _find_fastapi_validator(
5888	    path: str, method: str
5889	) -> Callable[[str, StarletteRequest], Awaitable[bool]] | None:
5890	    """
5891	    Find the validator for a FastAPI route that bypasses Flask.
5892	
5893	    This mirrors the _find_validator pattern used in Flask's _before_request,
5894	    returning a validator function for routes that need permission checks.
5895	
5896	    Args:
5897	        path: The request path.
5898	
5899	    Returns:
5900	        An async validator function that takes (username, request) and returns
5901	        True if authorized, or None if the route is handled by Flask (WSGI).
5902	    """
5903	    static_prefix = os.environ.get(STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, "").rstrip("/")
5904	    unprefixed = (
5905	        path[len(static_prefix) :] if static_prefix and path.startswith(static_prefix) else path
5906	    )
5907	
5908	    if unprefixed.startswith("/gateway/"):
5909	        return _get_gateway_validator(unprefixed)
5910	
5911	    if unprefixed.startswith("/v1/traces"):
5912	        return _get_otel_validator(unprefixed)
5913	
5914	    if unprefixed.startswith("/ajax-api/3.0/jobs"):
5915	        return _get_job_route_validator(unprefixed)
5916	
5917	    if unprefixed.startswith("/ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/assistant"):
5918	        return _get_require_authentication_validator()
5919

5921	    # raw path; prefixed artifact requests fall through to Flask, which owns their auth.
5922	    if _is_native_fastapi_proxy_artifact_path(path, method):
5923	        return _get_fastapi_proxy_artifact_validator(path, method)
5924	
5925	    if is_mcp_server_api_path(path):
5926	        return _get_mcp_server_validator(path)

5928	    return None

6052	def add_fastapi_permission_middleware(app: FastAPI) -> None:
6053	    """
6054	    Add permission middleware to FastAPI app for routes not handled by Flask.
6055	
6056	    This middleware mirrors the high-level logic of ``_before_request`` for routes that are
6057	    served directly by FastAPI (e.g., ``/gateway/`` and native artifact routes) and thus
6058	    bypass Flask's ``before_request`` hooks. It follows the same authorization flow:
6059	
6060	    1. Skip unprotected routes
6061	    2. Find the appropriate validator for the route
6062	    3. Authenticate the request (via custom authorization_function bridge or Basic Auth)
6063	    4. Resolve workspace context before validator execution
6064	    5. Allow admins to skip validators while still running after-request handlers
6065	    6. Run the validator for non-admins
6066	    7. Run after-request handlers on successful responses
6067	    8. Apply response filters for non-admins
6068	
6069	    When a custom ``authorization_function`` is configured, requests are authenticated by
6070	    constructing a Flask request context and invoking the custom function within it.
6071	    This bridges Flask-based auth functions into the ASGI middleware path without requiring
6072	    users to rewrite their auth plugins.
6073	
6074	    Args:
6075	        app: The FastAPI application instance.
6076	    """
6077	    # Snapshot native routes so the fail-closed check can tell them from Flask-delegated paths.
6078	    native_routes = _native_fastapi_routes(app)
6079	
6080	    @app.middleware("http")
6081	    async def fastapi_permission_middleware(request, call_next):
6082	        path = get_routed_asgi_path(request)
6083	
6084	        # Skip unprotected routes
6085	        if is_unprotected_route(path):
6086	            return await call_next(request)
6087	
6088	        # Find validator for this route
6089	        validator = _find_fastapi_validator(path, request.method)
6090	        if validator is None:
6091	            # Fail-closed (opt-in via MLFLOW_BASIC_AUTH_FAIL_CLOSED): deny a native FastAPI
6092	            # route with no validator. Flask-delegated paths pass through (authorized by Flask).
6093	            if (
6094	                MLFLOW_BASIC_AUTH_FAIL_CLOSED.get()
6095	                and _scope_matches_native_route(native_routes, request.scope)
6096	                and not any(marker in path for marker in _KNOWN_UNGATED_FASTAPI_ROUTE_MARKERS)
6097	            ):
6098	                return PlainTextResponse("Permission denied", status_code=HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN)
6099	            return await call_next(request)
6100	
6101	        # Authenticate using either the custom authorization_function (via Flask
6102	        # request context bridge) or the native FastAPI Basic Auth path.
6103	        try:
6104	            if auth_config.authorization_function != DEFAULT_AUTHORIZATION_FUNCTION:
6105	                auth_result = _authenticate_custom_for_fastapi(request)
6106	                if isinstance(auth_result, StarletteResponse):
6107	                    return auth_result
6108	                user = auth_result
6109	            else:
6110	                user = _authenticate_fastapi_request(request)
6111	        except MlflowException as e:
6112	            # Preserve Flask semantics for misconfigured custom auth plugins
6113	            # (e.g. unsupported return types) instead of collapsing to 401.
6114	            # Match Flask `catch_mlflow_exception` wire format (JSON body).
6115	            return JSONResponse(
6116	                status_code=e.get_http_status_code(),
6117	                content=json.loads(e.serialize_as_json()),
6118	            )
6119	        if user is None:
6120	            return PlainTextResponse(
6121	                "You are not authenticated. Please see "
6122	                "https://www.mlflow.org/docs/latest/auth/index.html#authenticating-to-mlflow "
6123	                "on how to authenticate.",
6124	                status_code=HTTPStatus.UNAUTHORIZED,
6125	                headers={"WWW-Authenticate": 'Basic realm="mlflow"'},
6126	            )
6127	
6128	        # Store user info in request state for downstream handlers (e.g., gateway tracing)
6129	        request.state.username = user.username
6130	        request.state.user_id = user.id
6131	
6132	        # The workspace-context middleware registered in ``create_fastapi_app`` runs
6133	        # *inside* this middleware (Starlette runs the most recently added middleware
6134	        # first), so the request workspace is not resolved yet when validators execute.
6135	        # Workspace-scoped lookups inside validators (e.g. resolving a gateway endpoint
6136	        # by name for the USE check) would fail and deny every non-admin request when
6137	        # workspaces are enabled. Resolve and set the workspace for the validator run,
6138	        # mirroring ``workspace_context_middleware``. Admins skip validators but still
6139	        # need this resolution so workspace-scoped after-handlers (e.g. MCP grant
6140	        # cleanup on delete) see the correct active workspace.
6141	        try:
6142	            workspace = resolve_workspace_for_request_if_enabled(
6143	                path, request.headers.get(WORKSPACE_HEADER_NAME)
6144	            )
6145	        except MlflowException as e:
6146	            return JSONResponse(
6147	                status_code=e.get_http_status_code(),
6148	                content=json.loads(e.serialize_as_json()),
6149	            )
6150	        workspace_context.set_server_request_workspace(workspace.name if workspace else None)
6151	
6152	        # Pre-read request body for after-request handlers that need it (the
6153	        # body is cached by Starlette so the route handler can still read it).
6154	        after_handler = _find_fastapi_after_request_handler(path, request.method)
6155	        if after_handler is not None:
6156	            request.state.raw_body = await request.body()
6157	
6158	        # Admins have full access: skip validators only. Flask's ``_before_request``
6159	        # similarly returns early for admins while ``_after_request`` still runs;
6160	        # mirror that here so delete cleanup (``_mcp_server_after_delete``) cannot
6161	        # be bypassed — otherwise recreating the same server name would restore
6162	        # previously authorized users' grants (CWE-862).
6163	        if not user.is_admin:
6164	            try:
6165	                if not await validator(user.username, request):
6166	                    return PlainTextResponse(
6167	                        "Permission denied",
6168	                        status_code=HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN,
6169	                    )
6170	            except MlflowException as e:
6171	                return PlainTextResponse(
6172	                    e.message,
6173	                    status_code=e.get_http_status_code(),
6174	                )
6175	            finally:
6176	                workspace_context.clear_server_request_workspace()
6177	        else:
6178	            workspace_context.clear_server_request_workspace()
6179	
6180	        response = await call_next(request)
6181	
6182	        if after_handler is not None and response.status_code < 400:
6183	            # After-handlers such as ``_mcp_server_after_delete`` use
6184	            # workspace-scoped grant sweeps; re-bind the workspace that was
6185	            # cleared before ``call_next`` (inner middleware uses a copied
6186	            # ContextVar context that does not propagate back).
6187	            workspace_context.set_server_request_workspace(workspace.name if workspace else None)
6188	            try:
6189	                after_handler(user.username, request)
6190	            except Exception:
6191	                _logger.exception("after-request handler failed for %s %s", request.method, path)
6192	            finally:
6193	                workspace_context.clear_server_request_workspace()
6194	
6195	        # Response filters are RBAC-based; admins retain unfiltered full access.
6196	        if not user.is_admin:
6197	            response_filter = _find_fastapi_response_filter(request)
6198	            if response_filter is not None and response.status_code < 400:
6199	                body = bytearray()
6200	                async for chunk in response.body_iterator:
6201	                    body.extend(chunk)
6202	                # Same ContextVar copy issue as after-handlers: re-bind workspace
6203	                # so RBAC predicates / backfill use the active workspace.
6204	                workspace_context.set_server_request_workspace(
6205	                    workspace.name if workspace else None
6206	                )
6207	                try:
6208	                    return _apply_fastapi_response_filter(
6209	                        response_filter=response_filter,
6210	                        username=user.username,
6211	                        body=bytes(body),
6212	                        request=request,
6213	                        response=response,
6214	                        path=path,
6215	                    )
6216	                finally:
6217	                    workspace_context.clear_server_request_workspace()
6218	
6219	        return response

class HostValidationMiddleware:
    """Middleware to validate Host headers using fnmatch patterns."""

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, allowed_hosts: list[str]):
        self.app = app
        self.allowed_hosts = allowed_hosts

    async def __call__(self, scope, receive, send):
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            return await self.app(scope, receive, send)

        if is_health_endpoint(scope["path"]):
            return await self.app(scope, receive, send)

        headers = dict(scope.get("headers", []))
        host = headers.get(b"host", b"").decode("utf-8")

        if not is_allowed_host_header(self.allowed_hosts, host):
            _logger.warning(f"Rejected request with invalid Host header: {host}")

            async def send_403(message):
                if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                    message["status"] = 403
                    message["headers"] = [(b"content-type", b"text/plain")]
                await send(message)

            await send_403({"type": "http.response.start", "status": 403, "headers": []})
            await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": INVALID_HOST_MSG.encode()})
            return

        return await self.app(scope, receive, send)


class SecurityHeadersMiddleware:
    """Middleware to add security headers to all responses."""

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp):
        self.app = app
        self.x_frame_options = MLFLOW_SERVER_X_FRAME_OPTIONS.get()

    async def __call__(self, scope, receive, send):
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            return await self.app(scope, receive, send)

        async def send_wrapper(message):
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":

def is_health_endpoint(path: str) -> bool:
    """Check if a path is a health endpoint that is exempt from host validation."""
    # Imported lazily to keep this shared module's own import graph light.
    from mlflow.server.handlers import _add_static_prefix

    # Health routes are registered via ``_add_static_prefix``, so under
    # ``--static-prefix`` they exist only at e.g. ``/mlflow/health``; the bare path
    # has no route behind it and would only 404. Match the registered form alone so
    # the exemption is never wider than the routes that exist. ``_add_static_prefix``
    # is the identity when no prefix is set.
    return any(path == _add_static_prefix(endpoint) for endpoint in HEALTH_ENDPOINTS)


def is_allowed_host_header(allowed_hosts: list[str], host: str) -> bool:
    """Validate if the host header matches allowed patterns."""
    if not host:
        return False

    # If wildcard "*" is in the list, allow all hosts
    if "*" in allowed_hosts:
        return True

    return any(
        fnmatch.fnmatch(host, allowed) if "*" in allowed else host == allowed
        for allowed in allowed_hosts
    )

def test_is_unprotected_route_handles_static_prefix(monkeypatch):
    # When ``_MLFLOW_STATIC_PREFIX`` is set, the health/static/favicon routes
    # are served from e.g. ``/mlflow/health``. Health checks must not require
    # auth on prefixed deployments.
    monkeypatch.delenv(STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, raising=False)
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/health")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/favicon.ico")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/static/foo.js")
    assert not auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/api/2.0/mlflow/users/list")

    monkeypatch.setenv(STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, "/mlflow")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/mlflow/health")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/mlflow/favicon.ico")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/mlflow/static/foo.js")
    # Unprefixed forms still pass through (local dev / non-prefixed deployments).
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/health")
    # Protected routes stay protected even with the prefix.
    assert not auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/mlflow/api/2.0/mlflow/users/list")

    monkeypatch.delenv(STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, raising=False)

1	"""
2	Native FastAPI routes for the server-info and health endpoints.
3	
4	Under uvicorn, every Flask request and every sync FastAPI endpoint runs on anyio's shared
5	default thread pool. When that pool is saturated (e.g. by slow artifact or search requests),
6	any endpoint waiting for a thread hangs, including capability discovery and health checks.
7	These routes avoid the shared pool: the health check answers directly on the event loop, and
8	the server-info payload is built on a small dedicated thread pool. The equivalent Flask routes
9	remain registered for deployments that serve the Flask app directly (Gunicorn, Waitress).

61	class _EfficientWSGIResponder(WSGIResponder):
62	    """WSGIResponder with O(n) body buffering instead of O(n^2) concatenation.
63	
64	    Starlette's WSGIMiddleware is deprecated and upstream has declined to fix the
65	    quadratic body buffering (see https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/2450,
66	    closed in favor of deprecating the module entirely).
67	
68	    Ref: https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/blob/0e88e92b592bfa11fd92e331869a8d49ba34b541/starlette/middleware/wsgi.py#L98-L117
69	    """
70	
71	    async def __call__(self, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
72	        # >>> Changed from original: use list + join instead of body += chunk
73	        chunks: list[bytes] = []
74	        more_body = True
75	        while more_body:
76	            message = await receive()
77	            if chunk := message.get("body", b""):
78	                chunks.append(chunk)
79	            more_body = message.get("more_body", False)
80	        body = b"".join(chunks)
81	        del chunks  # Free chunk list before build_environ copies body into BytesIO
82	        # <<< End of change
83	        environ = build_environ(self.scope, body)
84	
85	        async with anyio.create_task_group() as task_group:
86	            task_group.start_soon(self.sender, send)
87	            async with self.stream_send:
88	                await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(self.wsgi, environ, self.start_response)
89	        if self.exc_info is not None:
90	            raise self.exc_info[0].with_traceback(self.exc_info[1], self.exc_info[2])
91

93	class _EfficientWSGIMiddleware:
94	    """Drop-in replacement for starlette's WSGIMiddleware that avoids O(n^2) body buffering."""
95	
96	    def __init__(self, app: typing.Callable[..., typing.Any]) -> None:
97	        self.app = app
98	
99	    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
100	        if scope["type"] != "http":
101	            # WSGI cannot serve WebSocket (or other non-HTTP) connections. The Flask
102	            # app is mounted at the catch-all "/", so any WebSocket handshake that
103	            # isn't matched by a native FastAPI route reaches here. Reject it cleanly
104	            # instead of crashing. Sending websocket.close before accept is a valid
105	            # ASGI rejection (server maps it to HTTP 403); other non-HTTP scopes
106	            # (e.g. lifespan) are simply ignored.
107	            if scope["type"] == "websocket":
108	                await send({"type": "websocket.close", "code": 1000})
109	            return
110	        responder = _EfficientWSGIResponder(self.app, scope)
111	        await responder(receive, send)

210	async def _lifespan(app: FastAPI):
211	    # On startup, clean up assistant sandbox artifacts orphaned by a previous server generation:
212	    # containers whose in-process stream is gone, and stale per-session $HOME directories. Runs in
213	    # every uvicorn worker but only removes containers from a *previous* boot id, so it is safe
214	    # across workers. Note: this only runs under uvicorn (the default ASGI server); gunicorn and
215	    # waitress use the Flask app, which has no lifespan.
216	    #
217	    # Container reaping is NOT gated on the sandbox being enabled in this process: a server that
218	    # crashed with a sandbox container running and was restarted with the sandbox now off must
219	    # still reap that orphan, so it runs whenever a `docker` executable is present. The two reapers
220	    # run under separate error boundaries so one failing does not skip the other.
221	    if shutil.which("docker") is not None:
222	        try:
223	            from mlflow.server.sandbox import reap_orphaned_sandbox_containers
224	
225	            # Reaping does blocking Docker I/O; keep it off the event loop.
226	            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(reap_orphaned_sandbox_containers)
227	        except Exception:
228	            _logger.warning("Assistant sandbox container cleanup failed", exc_info=True)
229	    try:
230	        from mlflow.server.assistant.session import reap_stale_sandbox_homes
231

233	    except Exception:

235	
236	    # Remote mode but no sandbox means the assistant runs its work on the host; surface that once
237	    # at startup rather than silently, since it is a weaker isolation posture for a shared server.
238	    if MLFLOW_ENABLE_REMOTE_ASSISTANT.get() and not assistant_sandbox_enabled():
239	        _logger.warning(

241	            "(no `docker` executable found, or MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASSISTANT_SANDBOX=false); the "
242	            "assistant will run its Bash tool on the server host. Install Docker, or set "
243	            "MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASSISTANT_SANDBOX=true to require the sandbox."

258

260	    fastapi_app = FastAPI(

262	        description="MLflow Tracking Server API",
263	        version=VERSION,

265	        # FastAPI routers are mounted (otel, jobs, gateway, assistant, artifacts).
266	        docs_url=None,

287

289	    # This provides /gateway/{endpoint_name}/mlflow/invocations routes
290	    fastapi_app.include_router(gateway_router, prefix=static_prefix)
291	
292	    # Include Assistant API router for AI-powered trace analysis
293	    # This provides /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/assistant/* endpoints (localhost only)
294	    fastapi_app.include_router(assistant_router, prefix=static_prefix)
295	
296	    # Include native artifact upload/download router for ASGI streaming
297	    # This provides /api/2.0/mlflow-artifacts/artifacts/* and /ajax-api/2.0/... routes
298	    fastapi_app.include_router(artifact_router)

300	    add_mcp_exception_handlers(fastapi_app)
301	    for route_prefix in get_mcp_server_api_route_prefixes():

303	
304	    # Mount the entire Flask application at the root path.
305	    # Must come AFTER include_router so native FastAPI routes take precedence.
306	    fastapi_app.mount("/", _EfficientWSGIMiddleware(flask_app))

1	# Runtime fail-closed enforcement for the FastAPI permission middleware: a native
2	# FastAPI route with no validator is denied when MLFLOW_BASIC_AUTH_FAIL_CLOSED is on,
3	# while paths delegated to the mounted Flask app pass through untouched.
4	
5	from fastapi import FastAPI
6	from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse
7	from starlette.testclient import TestClient
8	
9	from mlflow.server import auth as a
10	
11	
12	async def _flask_like(scope, receive, send):
13	    # Stand-in for the mounted Flask WSGI app.
14	    await PlainTextResponse("flask-ok")(scope, receive, send)
15	
16	
17	def _build_client(monkeypatch):
18	    # No route resolves a validator, and nothing is "unprotected", so the fail-closed
19	    # branch is what decides native routes.
20	    monkeypatch.setattr(a, "is_unprotected_route", lambda path: False)
21	    monkeypatch.setattr(a, "_find_fastapi_validator", lambda path, method: None)
22	
23	    app = FastAPI()
24	
25	    @app.get("/api/3.0/mlflow/native-new-feature")
26	    async def native():
27	        return PlainTextResponse("native-ok")
28	
29	    app.mount("/flask", _flask_like)
30	    a.add_fastapi_permission_middleware(app)
31	    return TestClient(app)
32	
33	
34	def test_native_route_without_validator_denied_when_fail_closed(monkeypatch):
35	    monkeypatch.setenv("MLFLOW_BASIC_AUTH_FAIL_CLOSED", "true")
36	    client = _build_client(monkeypatch)
37	    assert client.get("/api/3.0/mlflow/native-new-feature").status_code == 403
38

41	    monkeypatch.setenv("MLFLOW_BASIC_AUTH_FAIL_CLOSED", "false")
42	    client = _build_client(monkeypatch)
43	    resp = client.get("/api/3.0/mlflow/native-new-feature")
44	    assert resp.status_code == 200

1	# Workspace Configuration
2	
3	Reference for the core flags, env vars, and startup checks for workspace mode. For setup and end-to-end flows, see [Getting Started](/self-hosting/workspaces/getting-started). For provider details and artifact routing options, see [Workspace Providers](/self-hosting/workspaces/workspace-providers).
4	
5	## Server Configuration (enable/disable)
6	
7	Enable workspaces with the flag:
8	
9	```bash
10	mlflow server \
11	  --backend-store-uri postgresql://user:pass@localhost/mlflow \
12	  --default-artifact-root s3://mlflow-artifacts \
13	  --enable-workspaces
14	```
15	
16	Or with env vars:
17	
18	```bash
19	export MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES=true
20	mlflow server \
21	  --backend-store-uri ... \
22	  --default-artifact-root ...
23	```
24	
25	Disable by restarting without `--enable-workspaces` after moving all resources into the `default` workspace.
26	
27	### Artifacts-only servers
28	
29	An artifact-serving-only deployment can validate and isolate artifact requests by workspace without
30	enabling tracking APIs. The artifact server must explicitly use the same logical workspace provider
31	as the tracking server:
32	
33	```bash
34	mlflow server \
35	  --artifacts-only \
36	  --enable-workspaces \
37	  --workspace-store-uri postgresql://user:pass@localhost/mlflow \
38	  --artifacts-destination s3://mlflow-artifacts
39	```
40	
41	`MLFLOW_WORKSPACE_STORE_URI` can be used instead of `--workspace-store-uri`. MLflow requires one of
42	these explicit settings in this mode because an artifact-only server has no tracking backend from
43	which to infer the workspace provider. The server initializes only the workspace provider; tracking,
44	model registry, workspace-management, and other non-artifact APIs remain disabled.
45	
46	Artifact requests continue to use `X-MLFLOW-WORKSPACE`. The provider validates an explicit workspace
47	or resolves its default when the header is absent. Unknown workspaces and requests without a
48	resolvable default are rejected before accessing artifact storage.
49	
50	### Admin Utility: migrate to default workspace
51	
52	To move all workspace-scoped resources into `default` to disable workspaces, use:
53	
54	```bash
55	mlflow db migrate-to-default-workspace <database_uri>
56	```
57	
58	By default, the command prints the rows to be moved and asks for confirmation. Use `-y` to skip
59	the prompt.
60	
61	Run a dry run first to surface conflicts and see how many rows will be updated:
62	
63	```bash
64	mlflow db migrate-to-default-workspace <database_uri> --dry-run
65	```
66	
67	Use `--verbose` to list all conflicts instead of a truncated sample.
68	
69	### Admin Utility: move resources between workspaces
70	
71	To selectively move resources from one workspace to another, use:
72	
73	```bash
74	mlflow db move-resources <database_uri> \
75	  --from <source_workspace> --to <target_workspace> \
76	  --resource-type <table_name>
77	```
78	
79	The `--resource-type` value is the database table name (`experiments`, `registered_models`,
80	`evaluation_datasets`, `webhooks`, `jobs`).
81	
82	:::note[Gateway resources not supported]
83	Gateway resources (`secrets`, `endpoints`, `model_definitions`, `budget_policies`) are not
84	supported by this command because they have inter-table foreign-key dependencies that make moving
85	them independently unsafe.
86	:::
87	
88	Filter which resources to move by name or tag:
89	
90	```bash
91	# Move specific experiments by name
92	mlflow db move-resources <database_uri> \
93	  --from default --to team-a --resource-type experiments \
94	  --name training-v1 --name training-v2
95	
96	# Move experiments matching tags (AND logic when multiple tags are given)
97	mlflow db move-resources <database_uri> \
98	  --from default --to team-a --resource-type experiments \
99	  --tag team=team-a --tag env=prod
100	```
101	
102	When neither `--name` nor `--tag` is specified, all resources of the given type in the source
103	workspace are moved. Tag filtering is supported for `experiments` and `registered_models` only.
104	
105	Use `--dry-run` to preview what would be moved without making changes, and `-y` to skip the
106	confirmation prompt. The command aborts if any resource name would conflict with an existing
107	resource in the target workspace.
108	
109	### Retargeting experiment artifact roots
110	
111	By default, moving an experiment preserves its stored `artifact_location`, so artifacts from new
112	runs keep using the pre-move storage path. Pass `--artifact-policy retarget` (experiments only)
113	to repoint every moved experiment to the artifact root resolved for the target workspace:
114	
115	```bash
116	mlflow db move-resources <database_uri> \
117	  --from default --to team-a --resource-type experiments \
118	  --name training-v1 --artifact-policy retarget \
119	  --default-artifact-root s3://mlflow-artifacts
120	```
121	
122	The target root comes from the workspace provider. A workspace-level `default_artifact_root` is
123	used as is, otherwise pass `--default-artifact-root` with the value the tracking server is
124	started with and the `workspaces/<name>` suffix is appended.
125	
126	Only the experiment's `artifact_location` changes, in the same transaction as the move. Artifact
127	objects are not copied or deleted, and stored run, logged model and trace URIs stay unchanged, so
128	everything already logged keeps resolving at its current location while new runs land under the
129	target workspace's artifact root.
130	
131	## Client Workspace Selection (summary)
132	
133	- Explicit: `mlflow.set_workspace("team-a")`
134	- Env var: `MLFLOW_WORKSPACE=team-a`
135	- Provider default: `get_default_workspace()` (SQL provider returns `default`)
136	
137	Clients send `X-MLFLOW-WORKSPACE` on REST calls; UI AJAX routes remain the same (`/api`, `/ajax-api`).
138	
139	## Startup Validation (when `--enable-workspaces`)
140	
141	- Tracking and registry stores must report `supports_workspaces() == True` unless the server is
142	  running in `--artifacts-only` mode, where those stores are not initialized.
143	- Workspace provider resolved (defaults to SQL-backed provider if none given)
144	- With `--artifacts-only`, the workspace provider must be configured explicitly through
145	  `--workspace-store-uri` or `MLFLOW_WORKSPACE_STORE_URI`.
146	- Reserved `default` workspace exists (created by migration)
147	- With `--serve-artifacts`, proxied artifact paths for non-default workspaces must include `workspaces/<workspace>/...`; legacy unprefixed paths remain valid for `default`.
148	
149	## Admin preflight for artifact roots
150	
151	Before enabling workspaces, confirm that existing experiment artifact locations do not already
152	live under the reserved `<default_artifact_root>/workspaces/<workspace>/...` path unless
153	they match the workspace layout you intend to use. If they do, move or rename those artifact
154	roots first to avoid collisions.
155	
156	## Artifact Behavior
157	
158	- By default, new experiments land under `<default_artifact_root>/workspaces/<workspace>/<experiment_id>`; runs inherit that path.
159	- Existing experiments/runs keep their stored locations (legacy unprefixed paths under `default` continue to work).
160	- To override the artifact root for a specific workspace, set `default_artifact_root` on the workspace (via `mlflow.create_workspace(...)` / `mlflow.update_workspace(...)` or the workspace REST API). When set, MLflow uses `<workspace_default_artifact_root>/<experiment_id>` (no `/workspaces/<workspace>` prefix) for new experiments in that workspace.
161	
162	## API Limitations
163	
164	- `create_experiment()` disallows `artifact_location` while workspaces are enabled; MLflow assigns workspace-scoped locations.
165	
166	## Detecting Workspace Support Programmatically
167	
168	- Call `GET /api/3.0/mlflow/server-info` to check `workspaces_enabled`.
169	- The endpoint is reachable without a workspace header; a `404` indicates an older server without workspace support.
170	
171	## Authentication Configuration for Workspaces
172	
173	When using workspaces with basic-auth (`--app-name basic-auth`), additional settings in the
174	[auth config file](/self-hosting/security/basic-http-auth#configuration) (`basic_auth.ini`)
175	control workspace-level permission behavior.
176	
177	| Setting                          | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
178	| -------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
179	| `grant_default_workspace_access` | `false` | When `true`, all users inherit `default_permission` for the reserved `default` workspace (pre-workspaces behavior). When `false`, users need explicit workspace permissions even for the `default` workspace. |
180	| `workspace_cache_max_size`       | `10000` | Maximum entries in the resource-to-workspace lookup cache used for permission checks.                                                                                                                         |
181	| `workspace_cache_ttl_seconds`    | `3600`  | TTL in seconds for cached resource-to-workspace lookups.                                                                                                                                                      |
182	
183	### `grant_default_workspace_access`
184	
185	This setting controls how the reserved `default` workspace interacts with `default_permission`.
186	
187	- **`false` (default)**: The `default` workspace does not inherit `default_permission`. Users must be
188	  granted explicit workspace permissions to access resources, even in the `default` workspace. This is
189	  the most secure option for new deployments.
190	- **`true`**: The `default` workspace inherits `default_permission` for all authenticated users. The
191	  `default` workspace also appears in `mlflow.list_workspaces()` results for every user.
192	
193	:::warning[Recommendation for existing instances]
194	If you are enabling workspaces on an existing MLflow instance that already uses basic-auth, set
195	`grant_default_workspace_access = true` for backwards compatibility. Without this, all existing
196	resources (which live in the `default` workspace) will become inaccessible to non-admin users who
197	lack explicit workspace permissions.
198	:::
199	
200	Example configuration:
201	
202	```ini title="basic_auth.ini"
203	[mlflow]
204	default_permission = READ
205	database_uri = sqlite:///basic_auth.db
206	admin_username = admin
207	# Required on first start (or set MLFLOW_AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD); MLflow ships no default.
208	admin_password = <strong-password>
209	authorization_function = mlflow.server.auth:authenticate_request_basic_auth
210	# Default secure setting for new deployments; for existing instances upgrading to workspaces,
211	# set this to true for backwards compatibility (see note above).
212	grant_default_workspace_access = false
213	workspace_cache_max_size = 10000
214	workspace_cache_ttl_seconds = 3600
215	```
216	
217	## Environment Variables
218	
219	| Variable                     | Description                                                                  | Default                                    |
220	| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
221	| `MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES`   | Enable workspace mode                                                        | `false`                                    |
222	| `MLFLOW_WORKSPACE`           | Active workspace for client operations                                       | None                                       |
223	| `MLFLOW_WORKSPACE_STORE_URI` | Override the workspace provider URI; falls back to the resolved tracking URI | None (falls back to resolved tracking URI) |
224	
225	`MLFLOW_WORKSPACE` chooses the target workspace. `MLFLOW_WORKSPACE_STORE_URI` selects where the workspace catalog lives (and which provider to use), not which workspace; if unset, the tracking URI is reused. Providers are discovered via the `mlflow.workspace_provider` entry point.
226	
227	## Next Steps
228	
229	- [Getting Started](/self-hosting/workspaces/getting-started) - Step-by-step enablement
230	- [Workspace Providers](/self-hosting/workspaces/workspace-providers) - Provider selection and artifact routing
231	- [Permissions](/self-hosting/workspaces/permissions) - Configure access control
232	- [Troubleshooting](/self-hosting/troubleshooting) - Common issues and fixes

def _is_known_ungated_route(path: str) -> bool:
    # Anchor markers to a segment boundary: "/mlflow/issues" matches "/mlflow/issues"
    # and "/mlflow/issues/..." but not "/mlflow/issues-other".
    for marker in _KNOWN_UNGATED_ROUTE_MARKERS:
        if marker.endswith("/"):
            if marker in path:
                return True
            continue
        start = 0
        while (idx := path.find(marker, start)) != -1:
            end = idx + len(marker)
            if end == len(path) or path[end] == "/":
                return True
            start = idx + 1
    return False

def _find_fastapi_validator(
    path: str, method: str
) -> Callable[[str, StarletteRequest], Awaitable[bool]] | None:
    """
    Find the validator for a FastAPI route that bypasses Flask.

    This mirrors the _find_validator pattern used in Flask's _before_request,
    returning a validator function for routes that need permission checks.

    Args:
        path: The request path.

    Returns:
        An async validator function that takes (username, request) and returns
        True if authorized, or None if the route is handled by Flask (WSGI).
    """
    static_prefix = os.environ.get(STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, "").rstrip("/")
    unprefixed = (
        path[len(static_prefix) :] if static_prefix and path.startswith(static_prefix) else path
    )

    if unprefixed.startswith("/gateway/"):
        return _get_gateway_validator(unprefixed)

    if unprefixed.startswith("/v1/traces"):
        return _get_otel_validator(unprefixed)

    if unprefixed.startswith("/ajax-api/3.0/jobs"):
        return _get_job_route_validator(unprefixed)

    if unprefixed.startswith("/ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/assistant"):
        return _get_require_authentication_validator()

    # `artifact_router` is not registered under `--static-prefix`, so this matches the
    # raw path; prefixed artifact requests fall through to Flask, which owns their auth.
    if _is_native_fastapi_proxy_artifact_path(path, method):
        return _get_fastapi_proxy_artifact_validator(path, method)

    if is_mcp_server_api_path(path):
        return _get_mcp_server_validator(path)

    return None

    Add permission middleware to FastAPI app for routes not handled by Flask.

    This middleware mirrors the high-level logic of ``_before_request`` for routes that are
    served directly by FastAPI (e.g., ``/gateway/`` and native artifact routes) and thus
    bypass Flask's ``before_request`` hooks. It follows the same authorization flow:

    1. Skip unprotected routes
    2. Find the appropriate validator for the route
    3. Authenticate the request (via custom authorization_function bridge or Basic Auth)
    4. Resolve workspace context before validator execution
    5. Allow admins to skip validators while still running after-request handlers
    6. Run the validator for non-admins
    7. Run after-request handlers on successful responses
    8. Apply response filters for non-admins

    constructing a Flask request context and invoking the custom function within it.

def _authorized_outside_before_request(req) -> bool:
    # Authorized outside a before-request validator: public allowlist, a
    # self-authorizing handler, or an after-request filter.
    path = req.path
    method = req.method
    # Suffix matching anchors on the API version prefix, so strip any configured
    # static prefix first (mirroring _find_fastapi_validator); otherwise public/internal
    # routes would wrongly fail closed under --static-prefix.
    unprefixed = _strip_static_prefix(path)
    if _matches_route_suffix(unprefixed, _PUBLIC_ROUTE_SUFFIXES):
        return True
    if _matches_route_suffix(unprefixed, _HANDLER_INTERNAL_AUTHZ_SUFFIXES):
        return True
    # Only response filters authorize a route on their own. Ownership grants and
    # permission cleanups run after an already-authorized write, so their presence must
    # not exempt a route that lacks a before-request validator from the fail-closed net.
    if AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS.get((path, method)) in _SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS:
        return True
    return any(
        pat.fullmatch(path) and m == method and handler in _SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS
        for (pat, m), handler in WORKSPACE_PARAMETERIZED_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS.items()
    )

def _before_request():
    if is_unprotected_route(request.path):

    authorization = authenticate_request()
    if isinstance(authorization, Response):
        return authorization

        raise MlflowException(

            f"'{type(authorization).__name__}'",

def is_health_endpoint(path: str) -> bool:
    """Check if a path is a health endpoint that is exempt from host validation."""
    # Imported lazily to keep this shared module's own import graph light.
    from mlflow.server.handlers import _add_static_prefix

    # Health routes are registered via ``_add_static_prefix``, so under

    # has no route behind it and would only 404. Match the registered form alone so
    # the exemption is never wider than the routes that exist. ``_add_static_prefix``
    # is the identity when no prefix is set.
    return any(path == _add_static_prefix(endpoint) for endpoint in HEALTH_ENDPOINTS)

def test_is_unprotected_route_handles_static_prefix(monkeypatch):
    # When ``_MLFLOW_STATIC_PREFIX`` is set, the health/static/favicon routes
    # are served from e.g. ``/mlflow/health``. Health checks must not require
    # auth on prefixed deployments.
    monkeypatch.delenv(STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, raising=False)
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/health")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/favicon.ico")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/static/foo.js")
    assert not auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/api/2.0/mlflow/users/list")

    monkeypatch.setenv(STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, "/mlflow")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/mlflow/health")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/mlflow/favicon.ico")
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/mlflow/static/foo.js")
    # Unprefixed forms still pass through (local dev / non-prefixed deployments).
    assert auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/health")
    # Protected routes stay protected even with the prefix.
    assert not auth_module.is_unprotected_route("/mlflow/api/2.0/mlflow/users/list")

61	class _EfficientWSGIResponder(WSGIResponder):
62	    """WSGIResponder with O(n) body buffering instead of O(n^2) concatenation.
63	
64	    Starlette's WSGIMiddleware is deprecated and upstream has declined to fix the
65	    quadratic body buffering (see https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/2450,
66	    closed in favor of deprecating the module entirely).
67	
68	    Ref: https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/blob/0e88e92b592bfa11fd92e331869a8d49ba34b541/starlette/middleware/wsgi.py#L98-L117
69	    """
70	
71	    async def __call__(self, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
72	        # >>> Changed from original: use list + join instead of body += chunk
73	        chunks: list[bytes] = []
74	        more_body = True
75	        while more_body:
76	            message = await receive()
77	            if chunk := message.get("body", b""):
78	                chunks.append(chunk)
79	            more_body = message.get("more_body", False)
80	        body = b"".join(chunks)
81	        del chunks  # Free chunk list before build_environ copies body into BytesIO
82	        # <<< End of change
83	        environ = build_environ(self.scope, body)
84	
85	        async with anyio.create_task_group() as task_group:
86	            task_group.start_soon(self.sender, send)
87	            async with self.stream_send:
88	                await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(self.wsgi, environ, self.start_response)
89	        if self.exc_info is not None:
90	            raise self.exc_info[0].with_traceback(self.exc_info[1], self.exc_info[2])

93	class _EfficientWSGIMiddleware:

105	            # ASGI rejection (server maps it to HTTP 403); other non-HTTP scopes
106	            # (e.g. lifespan) are simply ignored.
107	            if scope["type"] == "websocket":

141	def add_gateway_timing_middleware(fastapi_app: FastAPI) -> None:
142	    if getattr(fastapi_app.state, "gateway_timing_middleware_added", False):
143	        return

147	    @fastapi_app.middleware("http")
148	    async def gateway_timing_middleware(request: Request, call_next):
149	        if not get_routed_asgi_path(request).startswith(gateway_path_prefix):
150	            return await call_next(request)
151	
152	        # Reset the ContextVar so the handler task starts at 0. The handler task
153	        # inherits a copy of this context (Starlette's call_next uses copy_context),
154	        # so the reset is visible to send_request inside the handler.
155	        provider_call_duration_ms.set(0.0)
156	        start = time.perf_counter()
157	        response = await call_next(request)
158	        duration_ms = int((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000)
159	        # Read provider duration relayed via request.state by _record_gateway_invocation.
160	        # We can't read the ContextVar directly here because the handler runs in a
161	        # separate task and ContextVar mutations don't propagate back.
162	        provider_duration_ms = int(getattr(request.state, "gateway_provider_duration_ms", 0))
163	
164	        # For non-streaming responses, duration_ms covers the full round-trip.
165	        # For streaming responses, duration_ms covers only gateway setup time
166	        # (until the StreamingResponse object is returned, before the stream body
167	        # is iterated), so it reflects time-to-first-stream rather than total
168	        # streaming duration.
169	        response.headers[MLFLOW_GATEWAY_DURATION_HEADER] = str(duration_ms)
170	        if provider_duration_ms > 0:
171	            response.headers[MLFLOW_GATEWAY_OVERHEAD_HEADER] = str(
172	                max(0, duration_ms - provider_duration_ms)
173	            )

210	async def _lifespan(app: FastAPI):
211	    # On startup, clean up assistant sandbox artifacts orphaned by a previous server generation:
212	    # containers whose in-process stream is gone, and stale per-session $HOME directories. Runs in
213	    # every uvicorn worker but only removes containers from a *previous* boot id, so it is safe
214	    # across workers. Note: this only runs under uvicorn (the default ASGI server); gunicorn and
215	    # waitress use the Flask app, which has no lifespan.
216	    #
217	    # Container reaping is NOT gated on the sandbox being enabled in this process: a server that
218	    # crashed with a sandbox container running and was restarted with the sandbox now off must
219	    # still reap that orphan, so it runs whenever a `docker` executable is present. The two reapers
220	    # run under separate error boundaries so one failing does not skip the other.
221	    if shutil.which("docker") is not None:
222	        try:
223	            from mlflow.server.sandbox import reap_orphaned_sandbox_containers
224	
225	            # Reaping does blocking Docker I/O; keep it off the event loop.
226	            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(reap_orphaned_sandbox_containers)
227	        except Exception:
228	            _logger.warning("Assistant sandbox container cleanup failed", exc_info=True)
229	    try:
230	        from mlflow.server.assistant.session import reap_stale_sandbox_homes
231	
232	        await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(reap_stale_sandbox_homes)
233	    except Exception:
234	        _logger.warning("Assistant sandbox home cleanup failed", exc_info=True)
235	
236	    # Remote mode but no sandbox means the assistant runs its work on the host; surface that once
237	    # at startup rather than silently, since it is a weaker isolation posture for a shared server.
238	    if MLFLOW_ENABLE_REMOTE_ASSISTANT.get() and not assistant_sandbox_enabled():
239	        _logger.warning(
240	            "The MLflow Assistant is in remote mode but the Docker sandbox is not active "
241	            "(no `docker` executable found, or MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASSISTANT_SANDBOX=false); the "
242	            "assistant will run its Bash tool on the server host. Install Docker, or set "
243	            "MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASSISTANT_SANDBOX=true to require the sandbox."
244	        )

30	def resolve_workspace_from_header(header_workspace: str | None) -> Workspace | None:
31	    """
32	    Resolve (and validate) the active workspace given an optional header value.
33	
34	    When ``header_workspace`` is None or empty, the default workspace is used (if configured).
35	    Returns None if no workspace can be resolved.
36	    """
37	    store = _get_workspace_store()
38	
39	    if header_workspace := _normalize_workspace(header_workspace):
40	        if header_workspace != DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_NAME:
41	            WorkspaceNameValidator.validate(header_workspace)
42	        return store.get_workspace(header_workspace)
43	
44	    workspace, _ = get_default_workspace_optional(store)
45	    return workspace
46

48	def _get_workspace_store(workspace_uri: str | None = None, tracking_uri: str | None = None):
49	    """
50	    Resolve and cache the workspace store configured for this server process.
51	
52	    The store is constructed on first invocation using the provided arguments (or their
53	    environment-derived defaults) and memoized for all subsequent calls, regardless of any new
54	    ``workspace_uri`` / ``tracking_uri`` values supplied later.
55	    """
56	    if not MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get():
57	        raise MlflowException(
58	            "Workspace APIs are not available: workspaces are not enabled on this server",
59	            databricks_pb2.FEATURE_DISABLED,
60	        )
61	
62	    global _workspace_store
63	    if _workspace_store is not None:
64	        return _workspace_store
65	
66	    from mlflow.server import BACKEND_STORE_URI_ENV_VAR
67	
68	    resolved_tracking_uri = tracking_uri or os.environ.get(BACKEND_STORE_URI_ENV_VAR)
69	    resolved_workspace_uri = workspace_utils.resolve_workspace_store_uri(
70	        workspace_uri, tracking_uri=resolved_tracking_uri
71	    )
72	    if resolved_workspace_uri is None:
73	        raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(
74	            "Workspace URI could not be resolved. Provide --workspace-store-uri or set "
75	            f"{MLFLOW_WORKSPACE_STORE_URI.name}."
76	        )
77	
78	    _workspace_store = get_workspace_store(workspace_uri=resolved_workspace_uri)
79	    return _workspace_store
80

82	def _workspace_error_response(exc: Exception) -> Response:
83	    if isinstance(exc, MlflowException):
84	        mlflow_exc = exc
85	    else:
86	        mlflow_exc = MlflowException(
87	            str(exc),
88	            error_code=databricks_pb2.INTERNAL_ERROR,
89	        )
90	        # Preserve the original stack for debugging by chaining the exception.
91	        mlflow_exc.__cause__ = exc
92	
93	    response = Response(mimetype="application/json")
94	    response.set_data(mlflow_exc.serialize_as_json())
95	    response.status_code = mlflow_exc.get_http_status_code()
96	    return response

99	def resolve_workspace_for_request_if_enabled(
100	    path: str,
101	    header_value: str | None,
102	) -> Workspace | None:
103	    # The server-info endpoint must remain reachable even if the workspace header points to a
104	    # missing workspace, so skip workspace resolution entirely for this route.
105	    if path.rstrip("/").endswith("/mlflow/server-info"):
106	        return None
107	
108	    if not MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get():
109	        if (header_value or "").strip():
110	            raise MlflowException(
111	                "Workspace APIs are not available: workspaces are not enabled on this server",
112	                error_code=databricks_pb2.FEATURE_DISABLED,
113	            )
114	        return None
115	
116	    try:
117	        return resolve_workspace_from_header(header_value)
118	    except MlflowException:
119	        raise
120	    except Exception as exc:
121	        _logger.exception("Unexpected error while resolving workspace")
122	        raise MlflowException(
123	            str(exc),
124	            error_code=databricks_pb2.INTERNAL_ERROR,
125	        ) from exc
126	
127	
128	def workspace_before_request_handler():
129	    # FastAPI middleware may have already resolved the workspace for this request, and the
130	    # server does not set the env var so this should reflect request-scoped state.
131	    if workspace_context.is_request_workspace_resolved():
132	        return None
133	
134	    header_value = request.headers.get(WORKSPACE_HEADER_NAME)
135	    try:
136	        workspace = resolve_workspace_for_request_if_enabled(request.path, header_value)
137	    except MlflowException as exc:
138	        return _workspace_error_response(exc)
139	
140	    workspace_context.set_server_request_workspace(workspace.name if workspace else None)
141

143	def workspace_teardown_request_handler(_exc):
144	    if MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get():
145	        workspace_context.clear_server_request_workspace()

61	    # that only exist in the parent process.

75	def _cache_success_locked(key: str, response: ServerInfoResponse) -> None:
76	    _SERVER_INFO_CACHE[key] = _ServerInfoCacheEntry(
77	        response=response,
78	        expires_at_monotonic=time.monotonic() + _SERVER_INFO_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS,
79	    )
80	    _SERVER_INFO_CACHE.move_to_end(key)
81	    if len(_SERVER_INFO_CACHE) > _SERVER_INFO_CACHE_MAXSIZE:
82	        _SERVER_INFO_CACHE.popitem(last=False)

85	def _fetch_server_info_response(host_creds: MlflowHostCreds, endpoint: str) -> ServerInfoResponse:
86	    try:
87	        response = http_request(
88	            host_creds=host_creds,
89	            endpoint=endpoint,
90	            method="GET",
91	            timeout=3,
92	            max_retries=0,
93	            raise_on_status=False,
94	        )
95	    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - behavior validated by callers
96	        raise ServerInfoRequestError(str(exc)) from exc
97	
98	    if response.status_code == 200:
99	        try:
100	            data = response.json()
101	        except ValueError as exc:
102	            raise ServerInfoRequestError(f"Invalid JSON returned by {endpoint}") from exc
103	
104	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
105	            raise ServerInfoRequestError(
106	                f"Expected a JSON object from {endpoint}, got {type(data).__name__}"
107	            )
108	
109	        return ServerInfoResponse(status_code=200, data=data)
110	
111	    return ServerInfoResponse(status_code=response.status_code, text=response.text)
112

114	def _fetch_server_info_uncached(host_creds: MlflowHostCreds) -> ServerInfoResponse:
115	    return _fetch_server_info_response(host_creds, SERVER_INFO_ENDPOINT)

118	def _fetch_server_features(host_creds: MlflowHostCreds) -> ServerInfoResponse:

122	def fetch_server_info(host_creds: MlflowHostCreds) -> ServerInfoResponse:
123	    key = _normalize_server_info_cache_key(host_creds.host)
124	    with _SERVER_INFO_CACHE_LOCK:
125	        if cache_entry := _SERVER_INFO_CACHE.get(key):
126	            if time.monotonic() < cache_entry.expires_at_monotonic:
127	                _SERVER_INFO_CACHE.move_to_end(key)
128	                return cache_entry.response
129	            _SERVER_INFO_CACHE.pop(key)
130	
131	        if in_flight := _SERVER_INFO_IN_FLIGHT.get(key):
132	            leader = False
133	        else:
134	            in_flight = _InFlightRequest()
135	            _SERVER_INFO_IN_FLIGHT[key] = in_flight
136	            leader = True
137	
138	    if not leader:
139	        in_flight.event.wait()
140	        if in_flight.error is not None:
141	            raise in_flight.error
142	        return in_flight.response
143	
144	    try:
145	        response = _fetch_server_info_uncached(host_creds)
146	        with _SERVER_INFO_CACHE_LOCK:
147	            if response.status_code == 200:
148	                _cache_success_locked(key, response)
149	            in_flight.response = response
150	    except BaseException as exc:
151	        in_flight.error = exc
152	        raise
153	    finally:
154	        with _SERVER_INFO_CACHE_LOCK:
155	            _SERVER_INFO_IN_FLIGHT.pop(key, None)
156	            in_flight.event.set()
157	
158	    return response
159	
160	
161	def _clear_server_info_cache() -> None:
162	    with _SERVER_INFO_CACHE_LOCK:
163	        _SERVER_INFO_CACHE.clear()
